text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing wrist pain and difficulty moving your hand; I need to clarify the onset and nature of these symptoms to begin my evaluation. Did this start suddenly after a specific injury, or did it develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis.

Based on your description of pain in the right thumb and wrist radiating to the elbow, which worsens with holding an infant and improves with ice, this clinical picture strongly suggests De Quervain's tenosynovitis. The history of the fall may have contributed to the condition or caused a concurrent issue, but the specific radiation and aggravation by thumb/wrist movement are characteristic of this diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: X-ray of right wrist to rule out occult fracture from the prior fall or other bony pathology.
